scope: Exact static source subsets below only; entries are source records, not deduplicated semantic capabilities or claims of runtime availability. Most entries remain unreviewed. CAP-20 is incomplete.
routeReferenceBasis: catalog/operations.json and src/provider-probes.mjs at extraction; references indicate a bounded selected route slice, not equivalence or exhaustive review of the native record.

recorded-epic-catalog.scope: Recorded Epic catalog snapshot only; not a live registry, compatible engine guarantee, capability selection or semantic disposition. Each record is unreviewed and may overlap other inventories.

material-typed-wrapper-literal.scope: Static literal ueTool command names in non-test TypeScript files under src/tools/material at this exact pin; these are wrapper exports, not evidence of runtime registration or one-to-one public tools.
material-typed-wrapper-literal.method: List pinned git tree and read exact blob bytes; verify Git blob SHA-1, record SHA-256, strictly decode UTF-8, match exported literal ueTool(name, schema) expression. No upstream code imported, built or executed.
limitations: Seven source files are unmatched by the literal ueTool extraction. Six are separately inventoried as custom handlers; material-stats.ts is an internal helper. Actual runtime registration remains unverified.
Names may duplicate legacy sidecar entries; do not add counts or infer equivalence, loaded packs, schemas, effect, native behavior, licensing, or availability from this static subset.
material_set_param contains scalar, vector and texture variants; the existing Nexus strict routes are not automatically equivalent to every wrapper selector.
Typed routing and dynamic pack loading, dependencies and live native marker checks remain separate. No candidate is promoted or made callable by this artifact.

material-custom-handler.scope: Static handwritten material handler declarations and descriptor bindings at this pin; no runtime registration or native behavior inferred.
material-custom-handler.method: Read exact pinned source and registry Git blobs; compare SHA-256 and static declaration/descriptor lines without importing or executing upstream modules.

supportingSources.role: internal compile feedback helper; not a tool descriptor

limitations: The registry contains descriptor values and supports multiple routing modes; actual registered tools, loaded packs and schemas require separate runtime verification.
The helper formats optional compile feedback and is not itself a registered tool in this reviewed slice.
Paths and names may overlap legacy or ueTool surfaces; do not infer semantic equivalence or add source record counts as capability totals.

material_compile enforces exactly one material/function path; several other wrappers accept at least one without proving exclusive selection. Native behavior, persistence, licensing and failures need separate review.

ivan-unreal-mcp.scope: Literal Registry.Tool(TEXT(...)) declarations in the five pinned source files listed here; source identifiers are not reviewed contracts or runtime availability. This does not enumerate all source files or surfaces.
ivan-unreal-mcp.extraction: Read exact source bytes without compilation or execution; verify SHA-256, decode UTF-8, extract literal registrations and record source line numbers. The Blueprint file hash was independently matched to catalog/inventory-summary.json; other hashes are calculated from pinned GitHub source bytes.
limitations: This is a 23-declaration source subset, not the 26-declaration six-family audit total or complete standard editor inventory.
System, extensions, external MCP server, dynamic registrations and runtime-dependent exposure are not enumerated.
Declared tool names are not proof of route equivalence, eligibility, behavior, safety, licensing, or live availability.
Root and component licensing differ; no vendored RQL or Code-Exec source is copied or evaluated.
Console, Python and source mutation identifiers are inventory only: Nexus does not expose arbitrary execution or bypass existing authority boundaries.

claireon.scope: Server MCP visible-name filter and seven trace internal name declarations only. This is not a complete Claireon inventory, semantic disposition ledger, or Nexus allowlist.
claireon.extraction: Pinned GitHub recursive tree, per-file Git blob SHA-1 verification, SHA-256 recording, static literal extraction; no upstream code executed.
limitations: Other internal tools and registrations, proxy descriptors, conditional compilation, schemas and dynamic surfaces are outside this slice.
Internal names are not direct MCP tools; a reviewed fixed wrapper is required.
Records remain unreviewed and do not prove native qualification or contract equivalence.

internal-automation-trace-declaration.scope: Literal category and operation declarations for the two automation and two PIE trace internal tools in three exact pinned files; not a complete Claireon inventory or public MCP tool list.
internal-automation-trace-declaration.method: Read exact pinned source bytes without execution; verify Git blob IDs and SHA-256; match literal GetCategory/GetOperation definitions and record exact lines.
limitations: Internal declarations are not direct MCP tools or proof of runtime registration.
Schemas, dynamic registration, capability selection, ownership and live qualification remain separately reviewed.
Only the six documented static source subsets were enumerated; entries may overlap and counts are not comparable public tool totals.
UE live and extension behavior, Hayba dynamic packs and typed registrations, remaining Claireon internals and proxy, Ivan system/extensions and native runtime registration are not enumerated.
Unreviewed is not a selection, exclusion, callable operation or completed semantic disposition. CAP-20 must assign a specific task and candidate/review state after individual semantic comparison.
Catalog and source versions may change independently; verify hashes and route mappings before relying on this snapshot.
Hayba typed material wrappers are a separate static source surface; seven files in that group are explicitly unexamined. Matching names are not semantic equivalence or runtime registration.

entries.blockReason: The Windows launch path deletes a shared build-run log before spawning; at deadline it requests process termination and marks completion without a confirmed exit receipt.
entries.reopeningCondition: Review an explicitly owned build and output log, collision-safe launch lifecycle, process epoch and confirmed termination/cleanup before admission.

entries.blockReason: The native route can create a game target, accepts a resolved caller-selected archive directory, and starts asynchronous UAT packaging without a source-established caller ownership or physical destination boundary.
entries.reopeningCondition: Review a scoped host-authorized project, exact output destination, immutable job identity, completion and cleanup contract before admission.

entries.blockReason: The native process-global editor-session registry lists all job IDs when the selector is omitted and returns command line and archive path for a selected job without caller ownership or pagination; jobs do not survive restart.
entries.reopeningCondition: Review bounded, owner- and epoch-bound job observation with explicit unavailable/stale states and appropriate path disclosure before admission.

entries.blockReason: The handler treats a missing asset-registry entry as already deleted before checking for orphaned disk files; deletion and forced reference/editor effects require explicit authority.
entries.reopeningCondition: Review exact target and references, confirm registry and disk state, explicitly authorize force/editor effects and verify partial failure and no-rollback behavior.

entries.blockReason: The handler skips invalid or empty inputs and applies remaining deletes independently while returning an aggregate receipt containing refused and failed rows.
entries.reopeningCondition: Define per-input validation and exact targets, authorize destructive scope and force behavior, preserve each partial result and verify disk and recovery evidence.

entries.blockReason: The move handler delegates to rename, including its two selector forms, destination-exists no-op and possible world-external reconciliation without prior-object identity proof.
entries.reopeningCondition: Review move as a distinct identity-bound contract, bind source and destination before mutation and verify world-external effects, persistence and partial failures.

entries.blockReason: The handler accepts two selector forms and treats a missing source with an existing destination as a prior-success no-op without proving object identity; world rename can reconcile external packages.
entries.reopeningCondition: Bind source and destination identities at mutation time, distinguish selector forms and world-external effects, and verify persistence and partial failure without inferring success from destination existence.

entries.blockReason: The stock raw status response always returns ok:true, can mark Remote Control reachable even when the version value is absent, and infers remote-exec reachability from endpoint discovery without establishing editor process or project identity. Missing phase values are not an authoritative PIE state. Nexus uses a bounded internal preflight slice only with additional binding and marker checks; it is not a public canonical status operation.
entries.reopeningCondition: Review a fixed diagnostic contract that distinguishes unavailable and malformed channels, validates authoritative status and binds the exact editor, project, endpoints and epoch; require source, loaded-artifact and live evidence. Do not treat channel reachability or a marker alone as identity or qualification.

entries.blockReason: The direct pause wrapper selects an implicit game world without a session owner or exact PIE instance, can report ok even when no world exists, and reads phase through a getter that defaults missing ReturnValue to NotPlaying.
entries.reopeningCondition: Review a distinct owner- and editor-epoch-bound pause contract with exact PIE target, confirmed native phase, interruption recovery and live evidence; do not infer ownership or an effect from ok alone.

entries.blockReason: The direct resume wrapper selects an implicit game world without a session owner or exact PIE instance, can report ok even when no world exists, and reads phase through a getter that defaults missing ReturnValue to NotPlaying.
entries.reopeningCondition: Review a distinct owner- and editor-epoch-bound resume contract with exact PIE target, confirmed native phase, interruption recovery and live evidence; do not infer ownership or an effect from ok alone.

entries.blockReason: The public tool forwards a caller-chosen console command to the native console. Nexus forbids an arbitrary console escape.
entries.reopeningCondition: Do not admit this unrestricted record. A distinct fixed, bounded operation requires its own source-backed decision, authorization and native evidence.

entries.blockReason: The public tool forwards caller-supplied Python to editor remote execution. Nexus forbids arbitrary Python execution.
entries.reopeningCondition: Do not admit this unrestricted record. A distinct fixed, bounded operation requires its own source-backed decision, authorization and native evidence.

entries.blockReason: The world selector is ignored and enumeration is unbounded; the wrapper can return an empty list if the parsed body is missing actors. This is not an exact-world or complete bounded discovery contract.
entries.reopeningCondition: Review and qualify a bounded, explicit-world discovery contract with faithful errors, stable identity and native evidence.

entries.blockReason: The wrapper loads an object by path, converts non-JSON values to strings and returns per-property errors, without proving editor or PIE world identity or a bounded snapshot.
entries.reopeningCondition: Review and qualify a bounded, exact-object and explicit-world property read with typed output, error handling and native identity evidence.

entries.blockReason: The public surface accepts a caller-selected object path, property name and value without an explicit world, typed property contract, save scope or readback. Its wrapper may return ok after no parseable native output.
entries.reopeningCondition: Review a separate bounded typed property operation with explicit world and object identity, native preconditions, readback, persistence and failure evidence.

entries.blockReason: The public tool accepts a caller-selected object path, function and arguments and invokes that method through Python. Nexus forbids arbitrary backend and Python calls.
entries.reopeningCondition: Do not admit this unrestricted record. A distinct fixed, bounded operation requires its own source-backed decision, authorization and native evidence.

entries.blockReason: Both UI-composited and high-resolution variants lack exact PIE-world identity and use a time-derived shared temporary path without exclusive creation or an inline byte bound; UI capture reports requested dimensions and may fall back to the foreground window.
entries.reopeningCondition: Review UI-composited and high-resolution variants separately with explicit target/epoch, owned or bounded direct output, actual dimensions, bounded image delivery, interruption and native evidence.

entries.blockReason: A missing RC value can become successful empty logs, and subtracting the requested count before filtering does not guarantee the last N matching lines; ring gaps and response byte limits are not reported.
entries.reopeningCondition: Review a distinct bounded tail contract with attested process/project epoch, explicit missing and stale cursor errors, ring-gap reporting and bounded output evidence.

entries.blockReason: A missing RC value can become successful empty logs; the finite ring can overwrite older entries without a gap indication, and returned message bytes lack an explicit bound.
entries.reopeningCondition: Review a distinct bounded cursor stream with attested process/project epoch, missing-value refusal, explicit stale-cursor/ring-gap handling, bounded output and native evidence.

entries.blockReason: The direct key wrapper has no explicit editor/PIE-instance target; its shared Remote Control helper accepts a missing ReturnValue as success, and interruption during timed press can leave the release unconfirmed.
entries.reopeningCondition: Review a fixed target/epoch-bound key contract with confirmed acknowledgments, ownership, bounded duration and interruption-safe release evidence.

entries.blockReason: The direct mouse move wrapper has no explicit editor/PIE-instance target, and its shared Remote Control helper accepts a missing ReturnValue as success.
entries.reopeningCondition: Review bounded absolute and relative pointer contracts separately with exact target identity, validated acknowledgments and observable state evidence.

entries.blockReason: The direct mouse button wrapper has no explicit editor/PIE-instance target, and its shared Remote Control helper accepts a missing ReturnValue as success; press/release ownership is not established.
entries.reopeningCondition: Review exact target, confirmed button acknowledgment, ownership and interruption-safe release as a separate bounded contract.

entries.blockReason: The wrapper selects either Slate user or current viewport without explicit editor/PIE-instance identity; its shared Remote Control helper accepts a missing ReturnValue as success.
entries.reopeningCondition: Review separate exact Slate-user and gameplay-viewport contracts with bounded finite values, confirmed acknowledgments and release semantics.

entries.blockReason: The direct gamepad wrapper accepts Slate-user or viewport routing without explicit editor/PIE-instance identity; the shared helper accepts a missing ReturnValue as success.
entries.reopeningCondition: Review exact device/user and world target, finite ranges, confirmed acknowledgments and ownership/release semantics for separately scoped gamepad contracts.

entries.blockReason: The wrapper runs selected input steps in order without explicit editor/PIE-instance targeting or compensation; an unknown or failing later step can follow earlier effects, and the shared helper can accept a missing ReturnValue.
entries.reopeningCondition: Review a fixed bounded sequence with explicit target and owned resources, per-step effects, interruption recovery and unambiguous completion evidence; never infer rollback or replay.

entries.blockReason: The XR button wrapper has no explicit editor/PIE-instance target and its shared Remote Control helper accepts a missing ReturnValue as success; physical device behavior is not established.
entries.reopeningCondition: Review an exact synthetic-XR target, hand and action contract with trustworthy acknowledgment, owned release and native device evidence.

entries.blockReason: The direct pose wrapper can report ok:true with applied:false or missing native return value; it mutates a shared per-hand override without an ownership token or exact PIE-world attestation.
entries.reopeningCondition: Review a separately scoped exact-target and epoch-bound XR pose contract with verified application, exclusive ownership, release and timeout recovery; qualify the actual device/runtime.

entries.blockReason: The direct clear wrapper can report ok:true with cleared:false or missing native return value; it clears a shared per-hand override without proving who owns that override or the exact PIE world.
entries.reopeningCondition: Review a separate identity-bound clear/release contract with verified owner, target and completion, and explicit recovery for interrupted or foreign overrides.

entries.blockReason: Missing or false RC ReturnValue becomes an empty successful list, missing support flags default true, and descriptors and JSON schemas are materialized without an explicit result bound.
entries.reopeningCondition: Review bounded, target- and epoch-attested discovery with explicit incomplete/missing/error results, validated schema and support flags; this does not authorize arbitrary helper calls.

entries.blockReason: The public surface accepts a caller-selected helper name and arbitrary JSON arguments and dispatches the named native helper; Nexus forbids arbitrary backend calls.
entries.reopeningCondition: Do not expose this generic dispatcher. Review a separately fixed, bounded helper contract with its own authority, schema and native evidence.

entries.blockReason: The direct statistics wrapper defaults a missing native ReturnValue to empty text and returns ok with empty parsed metrics; it does not establish target editor epoch, metric freshness, completeness or a bounded raw response.
entries.reopeningCondition: Review a distinct bounded performance observation contract with explicit missing-data refusal, exact target and editor epoch, units and freshness, parsed-metric completeness and live source evidence; do not equate this with an owned trace capture.

entries.blockReason: The wrapper builds a console command from caller-supplied channels, writes a shared temporary path, and returns a fixed trace ID without establishing an exclusive output target or owned native capture.
entries.reopeningCondition: Review a distinct fixed-channel capture contract with authorized target, unique ownership, explicit output bounds, correlated native acknowledgment and failure recovery.

entries.blockReason: The wrapper accepts trace_id but does not use it to select or verify a capture; it issues global Trace.Stop and reports a fixed path without confirming which capture stopped.
entries.reopeningCondition: Review an identity-bound native stop contract that proves ownership before stopping and confirms completion; reconcile existing captures externally.

entries.blockReason: The common metric fetch always parses unit metrics even when fps is selected; the store treats corrupt or unreadable JSON as empty and save then overwrites the shared baseline file.
entries.reopeningCondition: Require complete, fresh group-correct measurements, explicit baseline ownership, atomic scoped persistence and refusal on unreadable or corrupt storage.

entries.blockReason: The metric fetch always parses unit metrics even for fps; comparison silently skips absent metrics and zero baselines, potentially reporting no regression with no meaningful comparisons.
entries.reopeningCondition: Require explicit group-correct metrics, freshness and a valid owned baseline; return incomplete rather than a passing comparison when required measures are missing or unusable.

entries.blockReason: The driver chooses the first top-level window by title substring, not editor PID/epoch; first-descendant name matching is ambiguous, and prior menu steps can expand or invoke before a later step fails.
entries.reopeningCondition: Define an exact attested window/process and unique target path, explicit partial-step receipt and interruption recovery before native qualification.

entries.blockReason: The driver chooses the first top-level window by title substring and reports only a boolean, without editor PID, project, epoch or ambiguity evidence.
entries.reopeningCondition: Define bounded exact-window discovery with process/editor epoch and ambiguity handling; retain substring existence as a distinct candidate.

entries.blockReason: Title substring selects the first matching top-level window; descendant enumeration has no explicit result or traversal bound and does not establish editor PID or epoch.
entries.reopeningCondition: Review bounded, exact editor/window identity and enumeration/truncation semantics with duplicate-title cases and live evidence.

entries.blockReason: Missing Remote Control ReturnValue is reported as unavailable, and the native reader chooses the first active PIE world and first controller without an explicit instance, while iterating text objects without an explicit cap.
entries.reopeningCondition: Require exact selected world/client and editor epoch, bounded enumeration, explicit missing-value errors and native observation before admission.

entries.blockReason: The wrapper starts a report without a caller identity and can supersede an existing machine-wide report slot; the resulting report path does not establish ownership.
entries.reopeningCondition: Require an atomic, explicitly owned report-session start with scoped storage and collision/refusal behavior; preserve existing reports.

entries.blockReason: The wrapper appends user-supplied assertions to the active process-global report without a caller or session ownership check; user-authored assertions are not native automation evidence.
entries.reopeningCondition: Require an explicit owned report handle and validate the caller and scope before recording; distinguish user assertions from independently observed results.

entries.blockReason: The wrapper writes a note to the active process-global report without identifying or verifying the caller or intended session.
entries.reopeningCondition: Require an explicit owner-bound report handle and mutation authorization, with scoped persistence and failure reporting.

entries.blockReason: The wrapper mutates the active process-global report without an owner or session selector; an omitted screenshot reference targets the most recent image.
entries.reopeningCondition: Require an owned report handle and explicit image identity, scoped persistence, and a reliable applied/not-applied result.

entries.blockReason: The wrapper finishes the active process-global report without a caller/session ownership check, and may stop any live PIE session before rendering; PIE cleanup exceptions are suppressed.
entries.reopeningCondition: Require an atomic owner-bound finish and separately authorized identity-bound PIE cleanup with confirmed outcome; never implicitly stop a foreign session.

entries.blockReason: The native wrapper accepts caller-supplied extra process arguments and map, uses configured or fallback executable/project paths, and does not confirm process cleanup after startup timeout. It does not establish a scoped launch or owned-process cleanup contract.
entries.reopeningCondition: Review a separate host-authorized launch contract with fixed arguments, attested executable and project, process epoch, endpoint identity, and bounded failure cleanup.

entries.blockReason: The wrapper registers a caller-selected port with no PID and no editor/project identity attestation; registration alone does not establish an authorized target.
entries.reopeningCondition: Review an explicit attachment contract with independently attested process epoch, project and endpoint ownership before any dispatch.

entries.blockReason: The process-local registry is unbounded and can include unverified port attachments; attached instances have unknown PID and liveness, with no attested process epoch or project identity.
entries.reopeningCondition: Review bounded discovery with explicit unknown, stale and unavailable results and independently attested process, project, endpoint and epoch; retain attached and launched instances as distinct states.

entries.blockReason: The wrapper suppresses termination errors, removes the registry entry and reports stopped without waiting for process exit; an attached entry may have no owned process.
entries.reopeningCondition: Review an owned-process stop contract that distinguishes attached and launched instances and preserves unconfirmed termination and cleanup.

entries.blockReason: This generic handler loads a caller-selected object and applies caller-selected reflected properties, marking its package dirty even when individual property writes fail. Its outer successful result may contain failed properties.
entries.reopeningCondition: Keep unrestricted reflection unavailable. A distinct fixed property operation needs an exact object identity, scoped typed properties, partial-result handling and native evidence.

entries.blockReason: The handler interpolates caller-supplied platform and configuration into an UnrealBuildTool command line and launches a background subprocess. Its initial running receipt does not establish completed output, bounded execution or process cleanup.
entries.reopeningCondition: A separately reviewed build contract needs fixed validated arguments, authorized target and output scope, bounded owned job lifecycle, correlated completion and native evidence.

entries.blockReason: The handler interpolates a caller-supplied platform into an editor cook command line and launches a background subprocess. Its initial running receipt does not establish completed output, bounded execution or process cleanup.
entries.reopeningCondition: A separately reviewed cook contract needs fixed validated arguments, authorized project and output scope, bounded owned job lifecycle, correlated completion and native evidence.

entries.blockReason: The handler starts project-file generation through a background subprocess and returns a running receipt before completion; the shared job launcher supplies no timeout to process capture. The record does not establish authorized output scope or owned cleanup.
entries.reopeningCondition: A separately reviewed generation contract needs explicit project and output authority, bounded owned job lifecycle, correlated completion and native evidence.

entries.blockReason: The handler resolves an editor actor by first matching object name and invokes a caller-selected zero-parameter BlueprintCallable function through ProcessEvent. Nexus forbids arbitrary backend calls.
entries.reopeningCondition: Do not admit this unrestricted record. A distinct fixed operation requires its own source-backed decision, target identity, authorization and native evidence.

entries.blockReason: The handler chooses the editor world, duplicates the first actor matching an object name and offsets the duplicate without an exact actor path or world epoch guard.
entries.reopeningCondition: Require reviewed exact actor and world epoch targeting, duplicate receipt and mutation semantics, and native evidence before admission.

entries.blockReason: The handler chooses the editor world and mutates tags on the first actor whose object name matches, without establishing an exact full actor path or world epoch.
entries.reopeningCondition: Require a reviewed native target identity and world epoch guard, bounded tag mutation semantics and native evidence before admission.

entries.blockReason: The handler resolves both editor actors by first matching object name, chooses the first skeletal or static mesh component, and attaches the actor without an exact actor, component and world identity guard.
entries.reopeningCondition: Require reviewed exact actor, component and world epoch targeting, attachment outcome semantics and native evidence before admission.

entries.blockReason: The handler calls spawn for up to 100 caller-supplied entries and returns an outer success containing separate spawned and error arrays, so a batch can partially mutate even when some entries fail.
entries.reopeningCondition: Review a separate bounded spawn operation with explicit world and target authorization, per-entry correlation, partial-result semantics and native evidence before admission.

entries.blockReason: The handler materializes recursive registry results before the 200-row output cap, optionally generates thumbnails, and returns no snapshot or indexing-readiness identity. Its output cap does not bound native enumeration or prove a complete consistent discovery snapshot.
entries.reopeningCondition: A distinct discovery contract needs bounded native work, exact result identity and explicit completeness or snapshot semantics, backed by source and native evidence.

entries.blockReason: The handler saves all dirty map and content packages and by default schedules editor exit; a deferred callback can cancel the exit after the initial response. This is broader than an exact authorized save target and does not establish completed shutdown.
entries.reopeningCondition: A separate operation needs explicit scope and shutdown authority, precise completion correlation, and source and native evidence; never infer authority from this record.

entries.blockReason: The handler forwards caller-supplied console text to GEngine Exec in the editor world and reports executed without checking its return value. Nexus forbids arbitrary console calls.
entries.reopeningCondition: Do not admit this unrestricted record. A distinct fixed operation requires its own source-backed decision, target identity, authority and native evidence.

entries.blockReason: The handler accepts an object-path form but truncates at the first dot and creates the package-derived object name without checking that the supplied object suffix matches it. It creates and dirties an in-session asset without saving, and checks for an existing object separately before creation.
entries.reopeningCondition: Require exact normalized package and object identity, an explicit unsaved-versus-persisted result, a reviewed creation-collision boundary and native evidence.

entries.blockReason: The Blueprint summary iterates all variables, components, function graphs, event nodes and interfaces into arrays without a native enumeration or serialized-response bound.
entries.reopeningCondition: Require a fixed bounded Blueprint inspection contract with exact identity, explicit truncation or snapshot semantics, and native evidence.

entries.blockReason: The handler resolves the Blueprint and optional parent by supplied names, mutates the SCS and reports component and short class names. Its receipt does not identify the resolved Blueprint path or resulting attachment, and no checked Blueprint state precondition is supplied.
entries.reopeningCondition: Require exact Blueprint, class and parent identities, a checked asset-state precondition, correlated resulting component and attachment receipt, and native evidence.

entries.blockReason: The handler removes the named SCS node and promotes its children, but the result reports only the component and Blueprint names; it neither carries a revision precondition nor reports the resulting child hierarchy.
entries.reopeningCondition: Require exact Blueprint and component identity, explicit child-promotion semantics, a checked state precondition, resulting hierarchy receipt and native evidence.

entries.blockReason: The handler adds a member variable with caller-supplied type and default text, but returns only the variable name and converted type; it does not return the resolved Blueprint identity, default value or checked prior asset state.
entries.reopeningCondition: Require exact Blueprint identity, typed and bounded default semantics, a checked asset-state precondition, correlated postcondition and native evidence.

entries.blockReason: The handler can retype and rename the named member in sequence, then returns a textual name summary without the resolved Blueprint identity, resulting type or a checked asset-state precondition.
entries.reopeningCondition: Require exact Blueprint and variable identity, checked prior state, explicit multi-step effect and partial-outcome semantics, correlated resulting type and name, and native evidence.

entries.blockReason: The handler imports arbitrary property text directly into the class default object and explicitly notes that a parse failure may leave the value partially written before returning an error.
entries.reopeningCondition: Require a typed and scoped property contract with exact Blueprint identity, checked preconditions, atomic or explicitly reported partial-write behavior, and native evidence.

entries.blockReason: The handler creates and registers a user function graph stub but returns only a name summary, not an exact resolved Blueprint or graph identity, checked prior asset state, or saved artifact.
entries.reopeningCondition: Require exact Blueprint and created graph identity, a checked state precondition, explicit stub and persistence semantics, correlated receipt and native evidence.

entries.blockReason: The handler either creates an event node or enables an existing disabled ghost, marks the Blueprint structurally modified, and returns only a name summary without an exact node identity, prior-state precondition or persistence receipt.
entries.reopeningCondition: Require exact Blueprint, event and node identity, a checked prior-state precondition, explicit create-versus-enable and persistence semantics, correlated receipt and native evidence.

entries.blockReason: The handler compiles a resolved Blueprint without a checked revision or editor context precondition, and collects all compiler messages and tokens into an unbounded result; its structured result does not identify the resolved asset.
entries.reopeningCondition: Require exact asset identity and revision or explicit staleness semantics, bounded diagnostics, compile ownership and completion correlation, and native evidence.

entries.blockReason: The handler selects the current editor world rather than an explicitly requested world or level, and its receipt returns the actor label and class name rather than an independently correlated exact actor and world identity.
entries.reopeningCondition: Require exact world and level targeting, stable actor identity and effect correlation, explicit persistence semantics and native evidence.

entries.blockReason: The whole tool dispatches a caller-selected command through GEngine::Exec in the editor world; arbitrary console execution is outside the Nexus public contract.
entries.reopeningCondition: Reopen only as a separately reviewed fixed operation with bounded arguments, exact target/authority and native receipt evidence; do not expose caller-selected console commands.

entries.blockReason: The whole tool accepts caller-selected Python code and helper include paths and executes through PythonScriptPlugin; arbitrary Python is outside the Nexus public contract.
entries.reopeningCondition: Reopen only as separately reviewed fixed wrappers with bounded inputs, explicit authority and native results; do not expose caller-selected code or includes, and verify component licensing.

entries.blockReason: The handler selects the active viewport, which may be a PIE view, and reads the full viewport pixel array before applying output dimension caps; it does not establish the selected viewport identity or a pre-read allocation bound.
entries.reopeningCondition: Require exact viewport targeting and a reviewed pre-allocation native capture and response budget with correlated image bytes and native evidence.

entries.blockReason: The handler selects the editor PIE viewport without a requested exact PIE instance or world and reads its full pixel array before output dimension caps.
entries.reopeningCondition: Require unique, attested PIE world and instance selection, a pre-allocation capture bound and correlated direct-byte response with native evidence.

entries.blockReason: The camera is resolved in the editor world from a label, name or path; the resolver returns the first matching actor or first case-insensitive label fallback without proving uniqueness, while the receipt names a label.
entries.reopeningCondition: Require exact unique world and camera identity, bounded capture and response limits, a correlated receipt and native evidence.

entries.blockReason: The isolated actor is resolved in the editor world from a label, name or path; the resolver returns the first matching actor or first case-insensitive label fallback without proving uniqueness, while the receipt names a label.
entries.reopeningCondition: Require exact unique world and actor identity, bounded capture and response limits, a correlated receipt and native evidence.

entries.blockReason: The source-file read uses a path-level Source directory containment check followed by a separate pathname read; the pinned source explicitly notes a junction/symlink replacement race. A returned-byte cap does not establish race-safe target ownership.
entries.reopeningCondition: Review a distinct bounded source-read contract with host-authorized exact target, handle-based containment and file identity checked at access, explicit truncation and fixture/native evidence.

entries.blockReason: The scaffold writes a header and cpp through separately checked pathnames; force can overwrite existing files and a later cpp failure deletes the just-written header, while the source jail is explicitly subject to a link-swap race.
entries.reopeningCondition: Require an authorized exact-file creation contract with race-safe containment, overwrite and partial-failure semantics, owned cleanup and native evidence.

entries.blockReason: The source update accepts caller content and a full-file or line-range write after a separate path-level containment check; a junction/symlink replacement race can change the target before the pathname operation.
entries.reopeningCondition: Review a separately authorized exact-file update contract with race-safe target/handle containment, version preconditions, scoped writes, partial-failure and recovery evidence.

entries.blockReason: The source delete performs an irreversible pathname deletion after a separate path-level containment check; a junction/symlink replacement race can change the target before deletion.
entries.reopeningCondition: Review a separately authorized exact-file deletion contract with race-safe target/handle containment, identity and ownership preconditions, explicit no-rollback behavior and native evidence.

entries.blockReason: The source listing gathers (recursively by default) all matching paths for every requested extension, sorts them and builds the entire response without a native enumeration or output bound; its path jail also has a documented link-swap race.
entries.reopeningCondition: Require a reviewed bounded source discovery contract with secure path containment, explicit completeness and pagination semantics, and native evidence.

entries.blockReason: The source compile can patch the running editor through Live Coding and, after failure or a non-start, fall through to a separate UBT invocation; the synchronous process call has no operation-specific timeout or owned process reconciliation shown.
entries.reopeningCondition: Require an explicitly authorized build contract with exact project and target, build ownership, bounded execution and output, no blind fallback after an uncertain outcome, and native evidence.

entries.limitations: A visible-name filter is not proof of live registration or permission. Search returns information about provider tools but does not itself execute them.
entries.blockReason: The raw search supports caller-supplied select lists that bypass max_results and return a full schema for each matched requested name, including repetitions. Category and empty-query modes scan the dynamic registry, and empty-query mode sorts matches before truncating. The stock schema has no query or category length limit or max_results upper bound. These behaviors do not establish bounded native work, output or an authorized complete snapshot.
entries.reopeningCondition: Review a separate fixed discovery contract with bounded selectors, native work and response bytes, explicit dynamic-registry and permission semantics, and source and live evidence.
